REASONS FOR DECISION

[1] The applicants make an Application to Reopen the claims for refugee protection.
DETERMINATION OF THE APPLICATION

[2] The Refugee Protection Division ("RPD") denies the Application to Reopen.

[3] I have reviewed the applicants' request to reopen their claims for refugee protection, and upon reviewing all of the relevant factors, including Refugee Protection Division Rules (Rules) 62 and 63 as well as the relevant case law, the following is my decision.
Background of RPD Claims

[4] A review of the Immigration and Refugee Board's (the Board) file indicates that the applicants (referred to as "the claimants" during the process of the claim) initiated claims for refugee protection upon arrival at the port of entry on XXXX XXXX, 2018 at the L.B. Pearson International Airport in Toronto. The two adult applicants completed a front-end examination with the assistance of a Romanian interpreter and were asked to appear for further examination on September 18, 2018. On that day, they were interviewed by an officer with the assistance of a Romanian interpreter and their refugee claims, including that of the accompanying minor applicant, were referred to the RPD on the same date.

[5] Several forms were completed with the officer, including the Generic Application and the Schedule A Background Declaration forms. The applicants were also provided with forms pertaining to their refugee claims, including Basis of Claim (BOC) forms on the same date.

[6] According to the Minister's Delegate Notes,1 Section 44 Report Review dated September 19, 2018, the applicants were provided with copies of all relevant documentation by hand and in person, including a Confirmation of Referral and Notice to Appear at the Immigration and Refugee Board at 74 Victoria Street, Toronto, Ontario. Regarding the time limit to submit the Basis of Claim (BOC) forms to the RPD, the Notice states that the RPD must receive the completed BOC no later than 15 days from the date on which the claim was referred.

[7] The Notice further states that if the RPD does not receive the completed BOC within that time, the applicant must appear on October 11, 2018 to explain why the BOC was late, or not yet provided. The Notice indicates that if the appellants do not appear on that date, their refugee claims may be declared abandoned and, if declared abandoned, the RPD will not hear the claims.
Applicants failed to submit completed BOCs and attend hearing on October 11, 2018

[8] The applicants failed to appear at the hearing scheduled for October 11, 2018. The RPD had received neither the completed BOCs nor any communication from the applicants to indicate that they were intent on proceeding with their claims for refugee protection. Given the applicants' failure to submit the BOCs, failure to attend as required, and failure to communicate with the Board, the presiding panel rendered its decision orally at the special hearing and, in accordance with section 168(1) of the Immigration Refugee Protection Act (IRPA),2 declared the claims abandoned on October 11, 2018.

[9] On October 25, 2018, a Notice of Decision was sent to the applicants regarding the fact that their claims had been declared abandoned as a result of the failure to provide completed BOCs and failure to appear at the special hearing on October 11, 2018.
Application to Reopen Claims

[10] On October 17, 2018, the Board received an Application to Reopen the applicants' refugee claims, along with a Use of Representative form from their counsel, and three completed BOC forms. The application included an affidavit from the principal applicant, wherein he states that he was not informed of the time limit to submit the BOCs or the special hearing date by the CBSA officer during the examination and referral of the claims on September 18, 2018.

[11] According to Rule 62(6)3 of the RPD Rules, the Division must not allow the application unless it is established that there was a failure to observe a principle of natural justice.

[12] I find that there has been no failure to observe a principle of natural justice on the part of the Board and therefore this application must be denied.

[13] The applicant states in his declaration that he was not informed by the interviewing officer that the he must submit completed BOCs to the Board within 15 days of the referral, and that the applicants must appear before the RPD on October 11, 2018 if they fail to do so. I find this explanation unreasonable and contrary to the documents on file. As stated above, the applicants received notification from the referring officer that their claims have been referred to the Board, their BOCs were due within 15 days, and that they would have to appear at a special hearing on October 11, 2018 if they failed to submit the BOCs by the due date.

[14] The applicants were assisted with the services of a Romanian interpreter during their initial front-end examination and during their subsequent referral interview; at no point did they indicate that they had difficulties understanding or communicating with the interpreter(s) in Romanian, the language of interpretation as per their confirmation.

[15] The applicant states in his request that he did not understand the requirements associated with BOC submission because he does not read English and has completed formal education at an elementary school level only. However, the examination and the referral interview were conducted with an accredited Romanian interpreter and the applicant was provided all documents pertaining to his and his family members' refugee claims at that time. There is no indication that the two adult applicants misunderstood the interpreter as answers provided to the questions asked are coherent and there is no indication of any difficulty. I find that the forms related to the three refugee claim were explained to the principal applicant and beyond that, the information was transmitted to him in writing in accordance with Rule 3(5)(a)4 of the RPD Rules.

[16] The applicant also states in his declaration that he was contacted by a person from the Board the day before the special hearing date of October 11, 2018, who informed him, through a friend who helped to interpret the message from English to Romanian, that the principal applicant was required to attend the hearing the following day. The applicant confirms in his declaration that he received this message from the Board but did not attend the hearing.

[17] I find that the principal applicant's failure to submit completed BOCs within 15 days of referral, his failure to attend the special hearing as required in order to provide a reason why the BOCs had not been submitted, and to explain why the claims should therefore not be declared abandoned, have not been reasonably explained, and there has been no breach of a principle of natural justice. In this case, I find that the applicants' failure to act in a diligent manner does not justify the reopening of the claims.

[18] For the foregoing reasons the request to reopen the claims of the applicants is denied.
(signed)
"M. Moc"
M. Moc
October 30, 2018
Date
1 Minister's Delegate Notes, dated September 19, 2018.
2 Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, S.C. 2001, c.27.
3 Refugee Protection Division Rules, SOR/2012-256.
4 Ibid.
